tasks.instruction: In the Fleet Analytics Console, an analyst arms the window-zoom tool and rubber-bands a span on the large primary chart to focus on one stretch of the run. The smaller charts beneath it are supposed to move with it and frame the same stretch of the run, but they don't: after the selection, those smaller charts settle on the wrong stretch of their own readings, so the panels no longer line up on the same moment the analyst framed on the primary chart. Fix the console so that selecting a span on the primary chart brings every linked panel to the stretch of its own readings that corresponds to the framed span. Do not change the fixtures, the number or layout of panels, the toolbox, or how the primary chart itself responds to the selection.

tasks.instruction:
The Artboard Editor loads a camera preset for the design surface and selects
the shape on it. The red selection frame and its corner handles are supposed
to hug the shape exactly as it appears under the current camera, and the zoom
readout should report the camera's zoom level.

On the orbit camera presets the selection is wrong: the zoom readout is off,
the selection frame is the wrong size, the corner handles do not sit on the
shape's corners, and on one preset the handles disappear entirely. The frame
also stays upright even though the shape looks tilted under the camera. On the
flat camera preset everything already looks correct.

Fix the editor so the zoom readout, the selection frame size, the corner
handle positions, and the frame orientation all match the shape as it is drawn
under every camera preset. Do not change the camera presets, the shape, the
scene feed, the protected profiles, or the verifier.

tasks.instruction:
The Notebook surface shows a short notebook of cells. Each cell has a prompt
gutter and an editor; code cells can also show an output below, and markdown
cells can show rendered text. Clicking a cell makes it active. Holding Shift
and clicking another cell is supposed to select the whole range of cells
between the active cell and the one you click, so you can act on several cells
at once.

There is a bug in the range selection. After you select some text somewhere on
the page and then Shift-click another cell, the range selection often does not
happen: only the clicked cell becomes active and the cells in between are not
selected. In some situations that is correct — when you are really extending a
text selection the browser should keep growing the highlighted text instead of
selecting cells — but in other situations the range selection should still
work and currently does not.

Fix the notebook so that Shift-click reliably extends the cell range selection
in every situation where it should, while still leaving the gesture to the
browser in the situations where the user is genuinely extending a text
selection. Explore the running notebook to work out which situations are which.
Do not change the notebook documents, the cell chrome, the scene feed, the
protected payloads, or the verifier.

tasks.instruction:
# Brine & Beam — received wall-chart schedules
The fictional yard delivered two approved refit charts. The mobile review app still
integrates a complete earlier refit. Repair the received-chart workflow so its live
schedule, full per-job ledger and critical-path/slip report agree with the foreman's
new drawings for **both** editions. This is an original standalone synthetic task,
not an upstream bug or a native Android/iOS app.

Open **Received chart**, choose each sheet, and use **Read at 85%**, pan and zoom.
**Reading guide** explains the day axis, arrows, bridges, lag ticks, all constraint
and report rules, and draft behavior. The sheets overlap; the charts are planned
dates, not a printed answer table. Use that evidence, not the older integration as
an authority. The same imported inbox exists in both evaluation conditions.

The app receives a deterministic external inbox in the prepared isolated runtime.
Outside it, an empty inbox is normal. All ordinary client source/build inputs are
available in this coding workspace; external attachments are product inputs, not
missing repository files. Rebuild/reset_to_scene makes a fresh review session;
ordinary reload preserves the saved edition and notes and does not re-import.

Preserve live edits to planned start/duration and incoming links (including changing
link type), slip preview, cycle/integration errors that do not disable the viewer,
Undo, Cancel, Save, notes, ordinary reload, independent editions, Reset, and inline
Export draft. Keep each job's planned start/duration/incoming set/earliest dates/float,
and the guide-defined report, human-readable in dedicated ledger/report sections;
keep a compact live schedule. Incoming links have no intrinsic order. Different
internal data structures, markup and framing are acceptable. Do not hardcode computed
totals or edit outcomes in place of implementing the disclosed scheduling contract.

Edit any ordinary app file listed by this task. `build.sh` alone is protected;
it checks ES modules and copies the whitelisted client files into mounted `dist`
without removing the mount. No dependencies or network services are required.
reasons: Outcomes are from the reviewed GPT-6 evaluation, not inferred from construction strata.
Protected external artifacts are visible through the running app only.
